messages:
maya.g: hey — i'm Maya, new on infra team. trying to get kubectl access to the prod cluster for a quick smoke test but running into permissions issues. ran `kubectl config get-contexts` and only see my local context.

maya.g: when i try `kubectl --context=prod get pods -n maya-dev` i get: 
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "maya.g@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "maya-dev"
```

maya.g: i followed the onboarding doc for kubeconfig but maybe missed a step. who should i ping to get the right role/namespaces?

lena.infra: welcome Maya! :wave: quick Q — did you run the SSO->kubeconfig flow? we don't hand out static kubeconfigs.

maya.g: i did `redwoodctl login` and got a success message, then `redwoodctl kubeconfig write --cluster=prod` which created a context called `redwood-prod`. `kubectl config get-contexts` shows it, but same forbidden error.

jonas.devex: hey Maya — two things to check: 1) SSO group mapping (we map Okta groups to k8s RBAC roles), 2) namespace binding (you may not be bound to maya-dev).

jonas.devex: run `kubectl auth can-i list pods --context=redwood-prod -n maya-dev` and paste output.

maya.g: output is `no` (same forbidden).

jonas.devex: ok. file a request in the infra access tracker and ping @lena.infra (or I can open it). The details we need: full username (maya.g@redwood.com), cluster (prod), namespaces (maya-dev), and desired role (dev: read/write). We'll add you to the Okta group `redwood-devs` which is bound to the `dev` ClusterRoleBinding in maya-dev.

mia.g: (typo) i mean maya.g — i'll drop the request now.

lena.infra: i've created a ticket for this: INFRA-4821 and added the ops rotation to approve. Will need approval from a team lead — cc @ryan.prodops.

ryan.prodops: approved the add for maya.g — infra, please propagate the Okta group.

infra-bot: INFRA-4821: Access grant applied — Okta group `redwood-devs` synced to cluster `prod`. RBAC: bound `redwood-devs` -> ClusterRole `dev` in namespace(s): maya-dev.

jonas.devex: after the sync, run `kubectl config use-context redwood-prod` then `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n maya-dev`. If still blocked, try `kubectl get rolebinding -n maya-dev` to confirm the binding exists.

maya.g: ok ran those — `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n maya-dev` now returns `yes`. `kubectl get pods -n maya-dev` shows my service's pods. woohoo 

maya.g: thanks everyone! super quick turnaround. :tada:

lena.infra: welcome again — if you need a namespace created for a sandbox repo, ping infra with repo name and approximate quota.

jonas.devex: added a short note to the onboarding doc to mention the Okta group mapping step so new hires don't get stuck on this.

maya.g: nice, that would've saved me 10 minutes. closing out my ticket. thanks all. :heart:
